payload.statement: A squeaking staircase step is usually caused by movement between two timber components rubbing together. As timber naturally expands and contracts with changes in humidity and temperature, small gaps can develop over time. When weight is applied to the tread, friction between the tread, riser, wedges or fixings can create the familiar squeaking noise. A squeak does not automatically mean the staircase has been poorly manufactured; it is often part of the natural movement of timber.

evidence.note: Why is my staircase step squeaking when I stand on it?

Q: Why is my staircase step squeaking when I stand on it?
A: A squeaking staircase step is usually caused by movement between two timber components rubbing together. As timber naturally expands and contracts with changes in humidity and temperature, small gaps can develop over time. payload.statement: One of the most common causes is slight movement between the tread and the riser. The tread may flex very slightly in the centre while remaining fixed at both ends by the staircase strings. This movement creates friction inside the groove where the riser fits into the tread, producing the squeaking sound.
